evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode="batched" with aggregation="weighted_mean" (scored/*/judge.toml lines 3 and 15/21); gates render/constraints use aggregation="all_pass" and are exempt. Each scored prompt carries explicit per-criterion independence and continue-after-failure wording: scored/functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles.' plus a setup-recovery rule (re-create setup on a new job when a setup step fails) and :7 'give that criterion its lowest score ... state what you observed, and move on'; scored/polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.'; scored/visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.' All three also say an evaluator/tool failure zeros only 'the unobserved outcome' and 'Preserve every completed independent observation' (functional:53, polish:18, visual:16). No stop-on-first-failure wording: grep of the prompts, app_context.md and criterion texts for stop/halt/abort/first fail/skip the rest found only the polish failed-send step's 'abort exactly one outgoing send request', which is a network-interception instruction, not a scoring stop. Row-local zero clauses (functional judge.toml:182 and :398 candidate-session control; polish judge.toml:23 and :32 'no update within 15 seconds ... this row is 0') zero only their own row on their own missing positive control, not siblings. The only all-criteria zeroing is the global browser gate (blank/static shell or failed server-backed create+independent readback), a precondition shared with the template, not one criterion's miss. Adversarial: a judge reading the functional prompt literally cannot zero all rows because M's move order failed; the sibling clause and setup-recovery rule forbid it. A conforming app that fails one protocol step (e.g. the full-Interview refusal in L) still has later protocols scored. Limitation: this row is a prompt-wording check and is fully decidable from source; no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope), so actual judge compliance with the wording is unmeasured but not required for this row.
